description: Raw ticks as persisted, one row per delivered Tick record. Written only by its owning service, which also owns this table's DDL and migrations; read by historical-query-svc as a declared read-side consumer. Evolution within this version lineage is additive only.

hypertable.rationale: recv_ts is the pipeline's event time and is monotonic per (provider, symbol), so chunks align with ingestion order. One day holds roughly 34M rows at the Phase-1 tick rate; the 7-day default would make a chunk large enough to hurt both compression and chunk exclusion.

columns.name: provider_symbol
columns.description: Optional on the wire, so nullable here.

columns.name: provider_ts
columns.description: The wire carries integer microseconds since the Unix epoch; timestamptz has exactly that resolution, so the conversion is lossless in both directions.

columns.name: recv_ts
columns.description: The hypertable's time dimension. Named recv_ts rather than ts because a Tick carries two timestamps and neither may be the implicit one.

columns.name: seq
columns.description: The contract's uint64 range exceeds signed bigint, but seq is session-scoped and resets on every adapter restart, so at any plausible tick rate it stays far below 2^63. Stored as bigint rather than numeric(20,0) to keep the column fixed-width and delta-compressible.

indexes.name: ticks_provider_symbol_recv_ts_idx
indexes.description: The documented access path: one provider's symbol over a time range.

notes: No unique constraint on the dedup key (provider, symbol, session_id, seq): TimescaleDB requires every unique index to include the partitioning column, and adding recv_ts to that tuple would enforce something other than the contract's key. Deduplication is the consumer's job, via tqtk_common.delivery.DeliveryTracker.
